figures.title: Quantization choices and execution paths
figures.caption: A quantization method, a numerical representation, packed tensors and a checkpoint container describe different parts of a deployment. The loader prepares a kernel-required runtime layout; compatible dispatch selects native FP4 math, fused dequantization or reconstruction. No compatible kernel means rejection; fallback is not guaranteed. Shown combinations do not assert universal interoperability.
figures.alt_text: Two distinct choices, error-control method and numerical representation, feed packed tensors enclosed by a checkpoint container. Loading and repacking prepare a runtime layout. Compatible dispatch branches to native FP4 math, fused weight dequantization such as W4A16, or higher-precision reconstruction. Unsupported combinations are rejected.

figures.title: Four-bit payloads and shared scale storage
figures.caption: Compact storage for the same 32 E2M1 values. OCP 1.0 MXFP4 uses one E8M0 scale byte; common 1D NVFP4 uses two E4M3 scale bytes plus a separate FP32 global scale per tensor. Bars are proportional only for payload and local scales. This is derived storage accounting, not a speed or accuracy comparison.
figures.alt_text: The MXFP4 row has sixteen payload bytes and one local scale byte, totalling seventeen bytes for thirty-two values. The one-dimensional NVFP4 row has sixteen payload bytes and two local scale bytes, totalling eighteen bytes, plus a four-byte global scale shared across the tensor.
